title: Morning Intel
bullets: Markets: Nvidia's reinstatement of Jensen Huang as CEO Monday sparked a furious rally — Nasdaq +6.5%, S&P 500 +4.7%, Dow +3% — with Nvidia shares up 31%, CoreWeave +22% and Micron +19%; Anthropic, which listed last week, slipped 1.4%.

Markets: Credit markets were less enthusiastic than equities — Nvidia's bonds dipped in price and spreads vs. Treasurys widened Monday, signaling bondholder unease that Huang's return could reaccelerate risk-taking.

Companies: Huang was rehired just 12 days after resigning amid a scandal tied to an alleged mistress linked to Chinese intelligence; the reinstatement followed a Trump-backed campaign, even as Nvidia's SEC accounting inquiry and internal probe continue.
Companies: Anthropic, fresh off a bumpy stock debut last week, is preparing a bond sale to help fund a planned ~$900B AI buildout; as an unprofitable company it's expected to be rated 'junk.'

Companies: M&A roundup — ABB buying Germany's Ziehl-Abegg for $2.22B; ConocoPhillips selling its Norway unit and UK Teesside stake to Vår Energi for ~$3.9B; TotalEnergies acquiring Continental Resources' gas assets; BASF selling its battery-recycling unit to Cylib.

Macro/Policy: UN COP31 climate talks in Turkey collapsed Sunday without a final deal after oil-producing nations blocked fossil-fuel-transition language, reviving calls to overhaul the summit process.

Macro/Policy: CMS proposed a Medicare Advantage overhaul cutting $107B in insurer payments from 2028-2037; week ahead brings Sept home prices and Nov consumer confidence data, plus Dell/Best Buy/Dollar Tree/Deere earnings.
